commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

1	# INDEX_RULES.md — Global Rules & Doc Routing
2	
3	**Doc link:** <https://github.com/brando90/agents-config/blob/main/INDEX_RULES.md>
4	
5	**TLDR:** Read this compact contract at task start, then read only the detailed rule sections whose triggers apply. All agents use the same policy; client-specific loading differs.
6	
7	## How to load these rules
8	
9	Refresh `~/agents-config` with `git -C ~/agents-config pull --ff-only` at each new non-trivial task and after an hour; preserve dirty/concurrent work and use the local copy if offline. Reread this index and relevant changed rules. When editing agents-config in an isolated checkout, use that checkout's index and detail files after refreshing the home checkout.
10	
11	All Hard Rule **Details** links and matching Trigger Rule/Guideline links are mandatory routing: **before the action they govern, read that detail section and its applicable workflow**, including secret overrides, spending and review decisions. Do not read every topic file. Rule numbers are stable; paths below resolve beneath `~/agents-config/` (or the active agents-config checkout). If files are unavailable locally, fetch the same path under `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brando90/agents-config/main/`. A Markdown link is a reading instruction, not proof the client loaded it. Never eagerly import this index or the detail collection into an entry file; read them as task files.
12	
13	Hard rules govern conflicts with older wording in a triggered procedure. Explicit user instructions and platform/tool constraints retain their normal precedence. The SNAP pre-approval in Trigger Rule 51 is scoped to authorized work and existing budgets. Detail pages retain the procedures, examples and exceptions; the catalog is optional lookup.
14	
15	## Hard Rules (every response, never skip)
16	
17	1. **Protect secrets.** Never commit credentials; inspect the exact staged diff and filenames before committing or pushing. Do not print secret values. Stop on a suspected leak and rotate exposed credentials; references/env vars replace embedded secrets. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-1)
18	
19	2. **Sync, then verify before pushing.** `git fetch` first; if upstream moved, rebase and re-test; never force-push a shared branch. Never fabricate unavailable source content; mark it unresolved. Inspect the diff and run the relevant deterministic checks. Report actual evidence and limitations, not an untested success claim. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-2)
20	
21	3. **Quality assurance (QA) is opt-in.** Only a tier Brando explicitly requests or sets for this work in a runbook, `[qa]`/`[light-qa]`/`[mega-qa]` commit tag or environment flag starts a model reviewer. Hooks, project files and older “QA required” text are not opt-in. “Do QA”/“light QA” means one opposite-company round; apply findings and verify without automatic re-review. Mega QA follows Trigger Rule 10. Hooks cannot impose unsolicited QA; do not mention QA when unrequested. Benchmark-reference acceptance (43) remains separate. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-3)
22	
23	4. **Response ending and titles.** Compact results: 1–2 sentences plus `.md`/`gdoc` links. End `**TLDR-end:** [proj: task]` with 1–2 sentences (`[proj]` without a task); never open `TLDR-start`. Emails/status reports also end `TLDR-end:` before any signature; include real decisions/deadlines only. Name and restate the core deliverable, not a micro-step (optional `›` suffix). Research updates open with a copy-ready status sentence; results also include a 1–2 sentence collaborator message in Brando’s voice. Match owned titles to verified summaries, identifier first. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-4)
24	
25	5. **Snapshot.** In chat, immediately after the closing summary, show `**Snapshot:**` with the smallest real artifact sample (normally 5–15 lines, at most 25), or say why nothing tangible exists. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-5)
26	
27	6. **Refresh configuration.** Follow the task-start/hourly refresh above, reread relevant changes, and preserve other owners’ work. Shared edits belong in both entry points. Review remains opt-in under Hard Rule 3. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-6)
28	
29	7. **Keep clients current.** Use the installed package manager and the supported update hook; never assume npm. Do not install/use the deprecated Gemini CLI. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-7)
30	
31	8. **Models, budgets and acceptance.** Masters: Codex `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra`; Claude `claude-fable-5-1` / `max`. Keep configured defaults; explicitly select proportionate execution workers (experiment selection: Guideline 19). Verify actual models/efforts and billing route (subscription or in-scope provider key). Never buy credits, enable new charges or weaken acceptance to recover. Required models/families and scientific pins remain binding. Before dispatch/review, read this detail and Rule 48. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-8)
32	
33	9. **Model access: CLIs, subscriptions and provider keys are allowed.** Agents may wire Brando's existing provider keys into agent clients, write provider application programming interface (API) calls and run key-loading scripts without asking. Load keys at runtime, never print or commit them, keep each within its owner's scope and existing budgets, and cap and cost-estimate key-billed batch or unattended runs. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-9)
34	
35	10. **Explain terminology.** Expand every acronym, metric symbol and project-specific term on first use in each response, chat included; use descriptive names, not opaque internal labels. For Brando, a code may lead if a short gloss follows on first use. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-10)
36	
37	11. **Numbers with verdicts.** Compact entries link full statistics (Rule 4). Give measured values, scales, denominators/splits, threshold sources, missing measurements. Statistical headlines need 95% intervals (resampling unit, limits) and `x [lo, hi] p-val=Z` (named test/null or `p-val=n/a`). Report correlations individually; when interpreting score levels, add absolute agreement and mean bias (judge minus human, positive = lenient) with both means. Give repeated-score variability/counts. Existing data only; read the statistics workflow first. Research precision (10-24-2026): read settings, definitions, numbers from the repo, run records or paper; `unknown` only after a named-path search (in caption). VeriBench tables carry a Pi + best open-weight row. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-11)
38	
39	## Trigger Rules (mandatory when triggered)
40	
41	Read the linked rule **before** its action. Multiple rows may apply. Stanford Network Analysis Project (SNAP) is the remote cluster; a pull request (PR) is a proposed Git change. PDF means Portable Document Format.
42	
43	| Rule | When → required action |
44	|---|---|
45	| [6](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-6) | Edit agents-config → keep shared entries/routes consistent; reread, verify, commit and push the owned change. |
46	| [7](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-7) | Create a PR → concise Summary and Test plan, relevant report/doc links; no unsolicited dashboard. |
47	| [8](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-8) | Checks and requested review pass → commit/push; unresolved critical findings or failed review block landing. |
48	| [9](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-9) | Launch graphics-processor work → estimate resources, assign devices, respect allocation approval/SNAP pre-approval, verify and clean up. |
49	| [10](rules/safety-and-models.md#trigger-rule-10) | Explicit Mega QA → three sequential review stages; preserve required model/family gates. |
50	| [11](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-11) | Requested QA passes and ultimate-utils reaches master → version, build and publish the package. |
51	| [12](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-12) | New session/background work → inspect existing workers; clean only >24-hour processes confirmed idle. |
52	| [13](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-13) | Research paper work or validity question → load research-writing guide; preserve evidence and source format. |
53	| [14](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-14) | New verified results, any agent/duration → chat ping + email including brandojazz and brando.science; verify/deduplicate delivery. Confirm routine pushes in chat. Email a push receipt only on request. |
54	| [15](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-15) | Substantive question → answer in chat; email only when explicitly requested. |
55	| [16](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-16) | Create/edit documents or save knowledge → headers; Google companion for findings; separate dated daily audience decks; verify. |
56	| [17](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-17) | Authorized task → finish relevant end-to-end work, verification and authorized publication; no smoke-only stopping. |
57	| [18](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-18) | Appendix/results/polish-only branch → inspect scope and land; substantive claims keep authorization. |
58	| [19](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-19) | Create/finish checkouts, merge branches or write in `~` → one canonical project; remove temp copies, run the sweep; no `~` clutter. |
59	| [20](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-20) | Lean proof/type-check task → discover pinned toolchain and actually compile; report observed output. |
60	| [21](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-21) | Paper introduction → load introduction and general research-writing guides. |
61	| [22](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-22) | Paper abstract → load abstract and general guides; preserve structural source comments. |
62	| [23](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-23) | Reader-facing prose → omit internal course/lab planning jargon. |
63	| [24](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-24) | Reader outside a subfield → translate ambiguous jargon and explain concepts first. |
64	| [25](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-25) | Personal blog → load personal-blog guides and reference posts; lab blogs use their separate route. |
65	| [26](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-26) | Email → BCC three Brando inboxes, use visible CC only on request; no ratings emails to collaborators without his yes; signature; plain takeaway. |
66	| [27](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-27) | Chat answer → plain direct first sentence, never an opening `A (TLDR)`/TLDR label (only `TLDR-end`); explainer-doc Q&A → `**A (TLDR):**` line. |
67	| [28](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-28) | Attached image/transcription → preserve original and provenance in the canonical project/experiment location. |
68	| [29](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-29) | Exact “Q go” plus screenshots → numbered question packet, original images, issue, verification and publication; review still follows Hard Rule 3. |
69	| [30](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-30) | Conference poster → load poster/research guides, compile and inspect rendering. |
70	| [31](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-31) | Lab paper blog/roundup → load lab-blog guide; draft in paper repo and obtain coauthor sign-off before publication. |
71	| [32](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-32) | Paper/release X thread → load thread guide; verify lengths, supported numbers and privacy gates. |
72	| [33](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-33) | Paper/release LinkedIn post → load LinkedIn guide; preserve numbers, author/privacy policies and review delivery. |
73	| [34](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-34) | Browser/account/form task → finish forms/files/sign-in; act on clear approval replies (including "I read it") to the pending checkpoint; verify. |
74	| [35](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-35) | Semantic paper-source edit → compile and commit fresh PDFs beside active paper sources; verify build and references. |
75	| [36](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-36) | Handoff/reusable/scheduled prompt → use the appropriate summary format; selection advice stays outside, execution facts inside; preserve schedule settings. |
76	| [37](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-37) | Long/dispatched run → maintain and publish live canonical results.md from launch; Markdown record + Google findings (Rule 16); dashboards opt-in. |
77	| [38](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-38) | SNAP connection or dispatch → check the official gateway before Cisco/Duo escalation; automatic reconnect is allowed with one shared five-host cooldown/backoff (never flood it); run relevant health preflight; token-spending checks remain opt-in. |
78	| [39](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-39) | Start/continue/finish experiment → canonical setup-named home/index, colocated artifacts, results tables in git, frozen evidence, lifecycle; research repos: no branches, straight to `main`. |
79	| [40](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-40) | Commit slide deck → fresh PDF, applicable text sibling and hash manifest in the same commit. |
80	| [41](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-41) | End substantive replies with a ranked `[p N/10]` list; start 9-10 items without spending or rule violations. |
81	| [42](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-42) | Dispatch beyond short lookup → owned checkout, named persistent session, verified launch/live records and completion watch; an agent in a numbered/stale session renames it to `<client>-<project>-<role>-<task>`. |
82	| [43](rules/safety-and-models.md#trigger-rule-43) | Benchmark reference edit → strongest-tier Claude AND Codex acceptance for every landed change; preserve attribution. |
83	| [44](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-44) | Long run, account/context/turn limit, or session end in an experiment folder → durable timestamped `CKPT_<task>.md`; update only on events: edit the ≤30-line state block, append one dated log line, never rewrite; exact continuation, verified handoff. |
84	| [45](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-45) | Ongoing coordinator → stable uniquely identified master checkpoint linking owned workers, watches and next commands. |
85	| [46](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-46) | Remote publishable phase → PR, exact-revision checks, requested review, immediate merge, receipt, safe sync. |
86	| [47](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-47) | Question about another agent → read its task context; distinguish chat activity, schedule and actual execution/results. |
87	| [48](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-48) | Dispatch or account/provider/context/turn limit → inventory authorized existing accounts; bound/verify handoff; keep one writer and scientific limits. “ac-scheduler” → host watch, master check-in, authorized notifications. |
88	| [49](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-49) | Research root layout/tidy → four content buckets and root allowlist; inventory live consumers before moves. |

# INDEX_RULES.md — Global Rules & Doc Routing

**Doc link:** <https://github.com/brando90/agents-config/blob/main/INDEX_RULES.md>

**TLDR:** Read this compact contract at task start, then read only the detailed rule sections whose triggers apply. All agents use the same policy; client-specific loading differs.

## How to load these rules

Refresh `~/agents-config` with `git -C ~/agents-config pull --ff-only` at each new non-trivial task and after an hour; preserve dirty/concurrent work and use the local copy if offline. Reread this index and relevant changed rules. When editing agents-config in an isolated checkout, use that checkout's index and detail files after refreshing the home checkout.

All Hard Rule **Details** links and matching Trigger Rule/Guideline links are mandatory routing: **before the action they govern, read that detail section and its applicable workflow**, including secret overrides, spending and review decisions. Do not read every topic file. Rule numbers are stable; paths below resolve beneath `~/agents-config/` (or the active agents-config checkout). If files are unavailable locally, fetch the same path under `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brando90/agents-config/main/`. A Markdown link is a reading instruction, not proof the client loaded it. Never eagerly import this index or the detail collection into an entry file; read them as task files.

Hard rules govern conflicts with older wording in a triggered procedure. Explicit user instructions and platform/tool constraints retain their normal precedence. The SNAP pre-approval in Trigger Rule 51 is scoped to authorized work and existing budgets. Detail pages retain the procedures, examples and exceptions; the catalog is optional lookup.

## Hard Rules (every response, never skip)

1. **Protect secrets.** Never commit credentials; inspect the exact staged diff and filenames before committing or pushing. Do not print secret values. Stop on a suspected leak and rotate exposed credentials; references/env vars replace embedded secrets. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-1)

2. **Sync, then verify before pushing.** `git fetch` first; if upstream moved, rebase and re-test; never force-push a shared branch. Never fabricate unavailable source content; mark it unresolved. Inspect the diff and run the relevant deterministic checks. Report actual evidence and limitations, not an untested success claim. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-2)

3. **Quality assurance (QA) is opt-in.** Only a tier Brando explicitly requests or sets for this work in a runbook, `[qa]`/`[light-qa]`/`[mega-qa]` commit tag or environment flag starts a model reviewer. Hooks, project files and older “QA required” text are not opt-in. “Do QA”/“light QA” means one opposite-company round; apply findings and verify without automatic re-review. Mega QA follows Trigger Rule 10. Hooks cannot impose unsolicited QA; do not mention QA when unrequested. Benchmark-reference acceptance (43) remains separate. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-3)

4. **Response ending and titles.** Compact results: 1–2 sentences plus `.md`/`gdoc` links. End `**TLDR-end:** [proj: task]` with 1–2 sentences (`[proj]` without a task); never open `TLDR-start`. Emails/status reports also end `TLDR-end:` before any signature; include real decisions/deadlines only. Name and restate the core deliverable, not a micro-step (optional `›` suffix). Research updates open with a copy-ready status sentence; results also include a 1–2 sentence collaborator message in Brando’s voice. Match owned titles to verified summaries, identifier first. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-4)

5. **Snapshot.** In chat, immediately after the closing summary, show `**Snapshot:**` with the smallest real artifact sample (normally 5–15 lines, at most 25), or say why nothing tangible exists. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-5)

6. **Refresh configuration.** Follow the task-start/hourly refresh above, reread relevant changes, and preserve other owners’ work. Shared edits belong in both entry points. Review remains opt-in under Hard Rule 3. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-6)

7. **Keep clients current.** Use the installed package manager and the supported update hook; never assume npm. Do not install/use the deprecated Gemini CLI. [Details](rules/maintenance.md#hard-rule-7)

8. **Models, budgets and acceptance.** Masters: Codex `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra`; Claude `claude-fable-5-1` / `max`. Keep configured defaults; explicitly select proportionate execution workers (experiment selection: Guideline 19). Verify actual models/efforts and billing route (subscription or in-scope provider key). Never buy credits, enable new charges or weaken acceptance to recover. Required models/families and scientific pins remain binding. Before dispatch/review, read this detail and Rule 48. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-8)

9. **Model access: CLIs, subscriptions and provider keys are allowed.** Agents may wire Brando's existing provider keys into agent clients, write provider application programming interface (API) calls and run key-loading scripts without asking. Load keys at runtime, never print or commit them, keep each within its owner's scope and existing budgets, and cap and cost-estimate key-billed batch or unattended runs. [Details](rules/safety-and-models.md#hard-rule-9)

10. **Explain terminology.** Expand every acronym, metric symbol and project-specific term on first use in each response, chat included; use descriptive names, not opaque internal labels. For Brando, a code may lead if a short gloss follows on first use. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-10)

11. **Numbers with verdicts.** Compact entries link full statistics (Rule 4). Give measured values, scales, denominators/splits, threshold sources, missing measurements. Statistical headlines need 95% intervals (resampling unit, limits) and `x [lo, hi] p-val=Z` (named test/null or `p-val=n/a`). Report correlations individually; when interpreting score levels, add absolute agreement and mean bias (judge minus human, positive = lenient) with both means. Give repeated-score variability/counts. Existing data only; read the statistics workflow first. Research precision (10-24-2026): read settings, definitions, numbers from the repo, run records or paper; `unknown` only after a named-path search (in caption). VeriBench tables carry a Pi + best open-weight row. [Details](rules/responses.md#hard-rule-11)

| [63](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-63) | “Text me” → WhatsApp self-chat via quiet verified route; confirm sent state and surface human-only linking. |
| [64](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-64) | Explicit weekly update → newest-first project folder, complete post plus appendix/images; publish and return full post/path; keep sealed data sealed; sync knowledge under Rule 16; preserve his task-list text. |
| [65](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-65) | Open files for Brando in an editor → one call `cursor -n <project root> <files…>` (new window for that project); never `-r` or per-file open prompts. |
| [66](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-66) | Brando's AI meeting notes (Fathom link/ID, "get my notes") → verbatim transcript first, then summary and action items; script-written byte-exact copies with provenance in the named folder; never retype or reconstruct. |
| [67](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-67) | Brief a worker, write a prompt or describe what an agent may do → default to allowed; state only binding limits, no precautionary bans or reassurance. |
| [68](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-68) | Create or copy a Google Doc/Sheet/Slides/Drive file → share "Anyone with the link" at creation: Viewer by default, Editor when readers fill it in; restricted only for secrets, sealed or private data. |
| [69](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-69) | Dispatch or wait on a worker → watch for death too (`scripts/watch_worker.sh`: done, dead, credit/limit-blocked, idle, timeout); on failure recover at once on the next eligible account (Rule 58). |
| [70](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-70) | Launch or finish an experiment or long job (training/eval, cluster/background job, or >~15 min; never chat turns) → `[RUN START] <name>` then `[RUN DONE] <name>: <status>` email; recipient copies per Rule 26, deduplicate with Rule 14. |
| [71](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-71) | Session start, shared state, or need the assistant → `agent_sync.py check` the SYNC.md, name conflicts; read `[FROM-UB9]` in the repo's inbox issue (#68); ask with `[TO-UB9]` + email. |
| [72](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-72) | Launch/resume a Vals-paid run → one large experiment at a time across projects (`valk` gate); queue, estimate cost; only Brando overrides. |
| [75](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-75) | Run pending, capped or failed on one cluster → try every reachable cluster yourself on empty GPUs, free hardware, no Duo; release idle. |
| [73](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-73) | Desktop session pins → only active or awaiting-Brando sessions, dated title; unpin sessions when done (never Projects, Rule 86). |
| [76](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-76) | Design, launch or interpret an experiment, benchmark, agent eval, scorer or parser feeding a reported number, or a surprising number → load `workflows/ml-research-practice.md`: predict every metric (incl. literal compliance) before running, trace one item, controls, look at the data. |
| [77](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-77) | Build, select, validate or deploy an LLM judge/grader/reward model, or a claim it "agrees with humans" → load `workflows/llm-judge-recipe.md`: input audit, label-reproduction test, controls, test once, ICC. |
| [78](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-78) | Write/submit an `sbatch` script on any Slurm cluster → `--mail-type=END,FAIL` to brando.science only (Brando, 10-29-2026); `BEGIN` only if long/key; one mail per array. |
| [79](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-79) | Sending/posting/saving anything a person reads (message, email, slide, Doc, README, PR) → spell-check it; Brando's surname is Miranda; check names against a source; quotes, identifiers and code keep their spelling. |
| [81](rules/maintenance.md#trigger-rule-81) | Verified work, any Brando repo → land on `origin/main` now; never park on a branch. |
| [80](rules/hosts.md#trigger-rule-80) | Launch/queue/size any GPU run, or free GPUs on mercury1/2 → use mercury as much as possible, whole node OK; empty GPUs only, never touch running jobs, shard big models over 4-5 A4000s, release when done. |
| [82](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-82) | Plan, run, score or report anything on public VeriBench → use the current release (`veribench@1.3`, 896 tasks, 10-28-2026); before each run `git ls-remote` veribench `main` and read its README release section; name the version beside every number. |
| [83](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-83) | Research/startup/eval with unknown need → ask if it should exist; run the quickest de-risking test locally, email results, write repo MD files; endpoints/logins in parallel; once it covers the main risk, push velocity. |
| [84](rules/research.md#trigger-rule-84) | Run/score/report vb-priv (or new VeriBench runs) → int_ref is the most important metric: run it once, save per-task results, derive int from it, lead updates with it. |
| [85](rules/writing.md#trigger-rule-85) | Write/edit/review ML research text (papers, reports, research Docs, updates) → load `skills/scientific-terminology`: one term per concept, reuse exactly, no stylistic synonyms. |
| [86](rules/workers.md#trigger-rule-86) | Claude app/claude.ai session start, Project change, new account sign-in, or Projects missing from the left → every Project of every account stays pinned in the sidebar; pin missing ones, run the session sync with `--all-accounts`, report counts; never wait to be asked. |
| [87](rules/responses.md#trigger-rule-87) | Report results, hand off, or send/change anything in Brando's name → load `skills/assistant`: label what ran (Lean/reading, DT, harness, model), short results-first, no branches. |

## Guidelines (best practices)

- [14](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-14): Complete direct authorized requests; do not ask again for already-authorized actions.
- [15](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-15): Read only task-relevant referenced docs.
- [16](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-16): Keep index, README and paths accurate; mirror shared entry bodies; verify actual host instruction files and reload state.
- [17](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-17): Use anchored paths in prose and commands.
- [18](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-18): Use `ls -la` for configuration/credential directories.
- [19](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-19): Select experiment models/judges by capability, total cost and validation; preserve pins.
- [20](rules/responses.md#guideline-rule-20): Messages/drafts as Brando use his concise first-person voice; email includes required routing/signature.
- [21](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-21): Check `~/keys/` for credentials, model-provider keys included, before asking; keep values transient.
- [22](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-22): Let the Node version manager control its path; avoid hardcoded versioned PATH entries.
- [23](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-23): Authorized email: Brando's signed-in account (mail connector, else uutils SMTP); BCC three inboxes, sender and To included; visible CC only on request; `drafted with <agent>` sign-off; “send” means send.
- [24](rules/maintenance.md#guideline-rule-24): Paper PDFs follow mandatory Rule 35.
- [25](rules/research.md#guideline-rule-25): VeriBench/VB private: >0.98 saturated; ≤0.9 good, ≤0.5 great, 0 best. "Harsh metric", N tasks, ASCII, harness. vb-priv: SYNC.md. Any metric ≥~0.98: solved (heuristic). [Set names](workflows/vb-sets.md).

## Authorized sign-in and verification codes

For an authorized account task, read [Rule 34](rules/services.md#trigger-rule-34): verify account, existing session or matching saved login and current challenge codes; keep credentials transient. Sign-in does not authorize unrelated transactions or messages.

## Machine Configs

Host routes: [catalog](CATALOG.md#machine-configs): [Mac](machine/mac.md), [SNAP](machine/snap.md), [Sherlock](machine/sherlock-agent-access.md), [FarmShare](machine/farmshare.md), [other agent clients](machine/agent-clis.md). Do not load unrelated hosts.

## Workflows

Use matching trigger links first. The [workflow catalog](CATALOG.md#workflows) indexes detailed procedures; [instruction maintenance](docs/instruction-audit/README.md) records the size budgets and client compatibility.

## Writing

The [writing catalog](CATALOG.md#writing) routes paper, blog and announcement work. Colocate all artifacts for a project/event; do not split them into top-level directories by file type.

## Abbreviations

`ac` = agents-config; `cc` = Claude Code. [Launcher/profile aliases](rules/services.md#abbreviations) are labels, not proof of account access or independent budget.

## Collaborators / Contact roster

Before addressing/assigning a person, resolve identity through [contacts](personal/contacts.md) and the [roster route](rules/services.md#collaborators--contact-roster).

202	    ).encode()
203	    archive_name = f"rating_packet_{round_id}_{rater_id}.zip"
204	    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
205	    packet_dir = output_dir / "rating_task_packet"
206	    for name, data in sorted(members.items()):
207	        destination = packet_dir / name

237	    }

243	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
244	    parser.add_argument("--cohort", required=True, type=Path)

"""Build a new, blinded rating packet from an explicitly frozen private cohort.

The coordinator supplies artifacts, hashes and terminal-output classifications;
this builder never selects by scores, runs a model, or edits existing packets.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
from urllib.parse import urlsplit
from zipfile import ZIP_DEFLATED, ZipFile, ZipInfo


EXPERIMENT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
COLUMNS = [
    "rater_name", "rater_id", "item_id", "task_folder", "candidate_file",
    "final_score_0_5", "ai_assisted_rating_attestation", "minutes_spent",
    "confidence", "rationale", "problem_note",
]


def digest(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def checked_file(record: dict, base: Path) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
    """Read only a real, hash-verified file; absence never becomes an empty answer."""
    require(isinstance(record.get("path"), str) and bool(record["path"]),
            "Every artifact needs an explicit source path")
    require(bool(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", record.get("sha256", ""))),
            "Every source needs a lowercase SHA256")
    path = Path(record["path"])
    path = (base / path).resolve() if not path.is_absolute() else path.resolve()
    require(path.is_file(), f"Missing source file: {path}")
    data = path.read_bytes()
    require(digest(data) == record["sha256"], f"Source hash mismatch: {path}")
    return data, str(path)


def permutation_key(seed: str, kind: str, identity: str) -> str:
    return digest(json.dumps([seed, kind, identity], separators=(",", ":")).encode())


def start_here(name: str, sheet_url: str, tasks: int, items: int, empty: bool) -> bytes:
    text = (
        f"# Main rating task: {items} files in {tasks} task folders\n\n"
        f"1. [Open your personal rating sheet]({sheet_url}) for {name}.\n"
        "2. Read [the scoring rubric](human_judgements_prompt.md) and "
        "[the short column guide](RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md). Compare formal specification "
        "statements (unproved theorem statements), not proofs.\n"
        "3. Follow the numbered task folders. In each, read `python_source/source.py`, "
        "the reference statements in `gold_lean/reference.lean`, and each file in `agent_lean/`.\n"
        "4. Enter `final_score_0_5` and `ai_assisted_rating_attestation` for each file. "
        "Please estimate `minutes_spent` and `confidence`. A one-sentence `rationale` is "
        "**preferred but optional**; use `problem_note` for issues.\n\n"
        "Your Sheet saves automatically; no copy or email return is needed. "
        "Use the included `ratings.csv` only if your invitation assigns the CSV route; "
        "it is an alternative form, not a second submission. Leave unfinished scores blank. "
        "If a reference prevents a rating, leave its score blank, add a problem note and "
        "email brandojazz@gmail.com. Notify Brando before changing completed ratings.\n"
    )
    if empty:
        text += "\nAn empty candidate file records an empty solver output. Apply the same rubric; no score is prefilled.\n"
    return text.encode()


def build_packet(cohort_path: Path, output_dir: Path, *, rater_name: str,
                 rater_id: str, sheet_url: str, task_ids: list[str] | None = None,
                 form_home: Path = EXPERIMENT) -> dict:
    """Create output_dir/rating_task_packet, its ZIP, and a private join receipt.

    Cohort schema: {schema_version:1, round_id, shuffle_seed, expected_artifacts,
    configurations:{id:{...}}, artifacts:[{task_id, task_description, item_id,
    configuration_id, python:{path,sha256}, gold:{path,sha256},
    candidate:{path,sha256,status:'nonempty'|'empty'}, provenance:{...}}]}.
    Item IDs have the neutral form '<round_id>__item001'. Per-task filenames and
    item IDs remain identical in subset packets and the complete packet.
    """
    cohort_path, output_dir = cohort_path.resolve(), output_dir.resolve()
    require(not output_dir.exists(), f"Refusing to overwrite existing build: {output_dir}")
    require(bool(re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", rater_id)), "Invalid rater ID")
    require(bool(rater_name.strip()) and rater_name == rater_name.strip()
            and not any(c in rater_name for c in "\r\n<>[]"), "Invalid rater name")
    url = urlsplit(sheet_url)
    require(url.scheme == "https" and url.netloc == "docs.google.com"
            and bool(re.match(r"^/spreadsheets/d/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(?:/|$)", url.path))
            and not re.search(r"[\s<>()\[\]]", sheet_url), "Use the personal Google Sheets URL")
    raw = cohort_path.read_bytes()
    cohort = json.loads(raw)
    require(cohort.get("schema_version") == 1, "Unsupported cohort schema")
    round_id, seed = cohort.get("round_id", ""), cohort.get("shuffle_seed")
    require(bool(re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{2,70}", round_id)), "Invalid round ID")
    require(isinstance(seed, str) and bool(seed), "A fixed shuffle seed is required")
    artifacts = cohort.get("artifacts", [])
    require(bool(artifacts) and len(artifacts) == cohort.get("expected_artifacts"),
            "Cohort count does not match expected_artifacts")
    configurations = cohort.get("configurations", {})
    require(isinstance(configurations, dict) and bool(configurations), "Missing private configurations")

    schema_path = form_home / "support/RATING_FORM_SCHEMA.json"
    schema_bytes = schema_path.read_bytes()
    schema = json.loads(schema_bytes)
    require(schema["columns"] == COLUMNS, "Current form schema changed; review the builder")
    require(schema["required_new_responses"] == COLUMNS[5:7], "Required fields changed")
    rubric = (form_home / "rating_task_packet/human_judgements_prompt.md").read_bytes()
    guide = (form_home / "rating_task_packet/RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md").read_bytes()
    require(all(field.encode() in guide for field in COLUMNS[5:]), "Guide lacks a response field")

    tasks, seen, pairs, loaded = {}, set(), set(), {}
    for artifact in artifacts:
        tid, item = artifact.get("task_id"), artifact.get("item_id", "")
        require(isinstance(tid, str) and bool(tid), "Missing task ID")
        require(bool(re.fullmatch(re.escape(round_id) + r"__item[0-9]{3,}", item)),
                "Use neutral, stable, new-round item IDs")
        require(item not in seen, "Duplicate item ID")
        seen.add(item)
        require(artifact.get("configuration_id") in configurations, "Unknown configuration ID")
        pair = (tid, artifact["configuration_id"])
        require(pair not in pairs, "Duplicate task/configuration cell")
        pairs.add(pair)
        description = artifact.get("task_description", "")
        require(isinstance(description, str) and bool(description.strip()), "Missing task description")
        slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", description.lower()).strip("_")[:80]
        require(bool(slug), "Task description needs a readable name")
        py, py_path = checked_file(artifact["python"], cohort_path.parent)
        gold, gold_path = checked_file(artifact["gold"], cohort_path.parent)
        candidate, candidate_path = checked_file(artifact["candidate"], cohort_path.parent)
        status = artifact["candidate"].get("status")
        require(status in ("nonempty", "empty"), "Candidate status must be nonempty or empty")
        require((status == "empty") == (len(candidate) == 0), "Candidate status contradicts bytes")
        require(bool(py) and bool(gold), "Python and reference must be nonempty")
        task = tasks.setdefault(tid, {"description": description, "slug": slug,
                                     "python": py, "gold": gold, "items": []})
        require((task["description"], task["python"], task["gold"]) == (description, py, gold),
                "One task has inconsistent source/reference/description")
        task["items"].append(artifact)
        loaded[item] = {"data": candidate, "source_paths": {
            "python": py_path, "gold": gold_path, "candidate": candidate_path}}

    selected = set(tasks) if task_ids is None else set(task_ids)
    require(bool(selected) and selected <= set(tasks), "Unknown or empty assigned task subset")
    require(task_ids is None or len(selected) == len(task_ids), "Duplicate assigned task ID")
    ordered_tasks = sorted(tasks, key=lambda tid: permutation_key(seed, "task", tid))
    members, response_rows, joins = {}, [], []
    for number, tid in enumerate(ordered_tasks, 1):
        if tid not in selected:
            continue
        task = tasks[tid]
        folder = f"task_{number:02d}_{task['slug']}"
        members[f"{folder}/python_source/source.py"] = task["python"]
        members[f"{folder}/gold_lean/reference.lean"] = task["gold"]
        ordered_items = sorted(task["items"], key=lambda a: permutation_key(seed, "candidate", a["item_id"]))
        for index, artifact in enumerate(ordered_items, 1):
            item = artifact["item_id"]
            candidate_name = f"{folder}/agent_lean/agent_{index}.lean"
            members[candidate_name] = loaded[item]["data"]
            response_rows.append(dict(zip(COLUMNS[:5], [rater_name, rater_id, item, folder, candidate_name])))
            hashes = {k: artifact[k]["sha256"] for k in ("python", "gold", "candidate")}
            content_key = digest(json.dumps({"task_id": tid, **hashes}, sort_keys=True).encode())
            joins.append({"round_id": round_id, "rater_id": rater_id, "item_id": item,
                          "task_id": tid, "task_folder": folder, "candidate_file": candidate_name,
                          "configuration_id": artifact["configuration_id"],
                          "candidate_status": artifact["candidate"]["status"],
                          "hashes": hashes, "source_paths": loaded[item]["source_paths"],
                          "payload_content_key": content_key,
                          "observation_key": [round_id, rater_id, item],
                          "provenance": artifact.get("provenance", {})})

    members["START_HERE.md"] = start_here(rater_name, sheet_url, len(selected), len(joins),
                                           any(j["candidate_status"] == "empty" for j in joins))
    members["human_judgements_prompt.md"] = rubric
    members["RATING_FORM_GUIDE.md"] = guide
    sheet = io.StringIO(newline="")
    writer = csv.DictWriter(sheet, fieldnames=COLUMNS, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(response_rows)
    members["ratings.csv"] = sheet.getvalue().encode()
    # Refuse known identity leaks; never redact or rewrite scientific input bytes.
    labels = "\n".join(members) + "\n" + sheet.getvalue()
    for config_id, config in configurations.items():
        tokens = [config_id, config.get("model", ""), config.get("harness", ""),
                  *config.get("identity_tokens", [])]
        require(all(isinstance(token, str) for token in tokens), "Identity tokens must be strings")
        require(not any(len(token) >= 4 and token.lower() in labels.lower() for token in tokens),
                "A generated participant label exposes a configuration identity")
        require(not any(len(token) >= 4 and token.lower().encode() in data.lower()
                        for token in tokens for data in members.values()),
                "Participant payload contains a known configuration identity; resolve without rewriting candidate bytes")
    members["FILES.sha256"] = "".join(
        f"{digest(data)}  {name}\n" for name, data in sorted(members.items())
    ).encode()
    archive_name = f"rating_packet_{round_id}_{rater_id}.zip"
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    packet_dir = output_dir / "rating_task_packet"
    for name, data in sorted(members.items()):
        destination = packet_dir / name
        destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        destination.write_bytes(data)
    archive_path = output_dir / archive_name
    with ZipFile(archive_path, "x", compression=ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=9) as archive:
        for name, data in sorted(members.items()):
            info = ZipInfo(name, date_time=(1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0))
            info.create_system = 3
            info.external_attr = 0o100644 << 16
            info.compress_type = ZIP_DEFLATED
            archive.writestr(info, data, compress_type=ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=9)
    with ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
        require(set(archive.namelist()) == set(members), "Archive member mismatch")
        for name, data in members.items():
            require(archive.read(name) == data and (packet_dir / name).read_bytes() == data,
                    "Packaged bytes changed")
    receipt = {
        "schema_version": 1, "status": "BUILT_VERIFIED_NOT_SENT", "round_id": round_id,
        "cohort_path": str(cohort_path), "cohort_sha256": digest(raw), "shuffle_seed": seed,
        "rater_name": rater_name, "rater_id": rater_id, "sheet_url": sheet_url,
        "task_count": len(selected), "artifact_count": len(joins),
        "empty_artifact_count": sum(j["candidate_status"] == "empty" for j in joins),
        "packet_directory": str(packet_dir), "archive_path": str(archive_path),
        "archive_sha256": digest(archive_path.read_bytes()),
        "files_manifest_sha256": digest(members["FILES.sha256"]),
        "form_schema_version": schema["version"], "form_schema_sha256": digest(schema_bytes),
        "rubric_sha256": digest(rubric), "guide_sha256": digest(guide),
        "configurations": configurations, "artifact_joins": joins,
        "deduplication": "Use observation_key for repeated exports/subset copies; preserve provenance for historical joins. Packet copies are not new ratings.",
        "identity_scope": "Coordinator-only receipt. Labels are neutral and known model/harness/identity tokens are checked. Scientific bytes are unchanged; literal-token checks do not establish absence of every indirect authorship cue.",
    }
    (output_dir / "ASSEMBLY_RECEIPT.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + "\n")
    return receipt


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--cohort", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True, type=Path, help="New private build directory; must not exist")
    parser.add_argument("--rater-name", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--rater-id", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--sheet-url", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tasks", nargs="+", help="Assigned task IDs; omit for the full cohort")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    receipt = build_packet(args.cohort, args.output_dir, rater_name=args.rater_name,
                           rater_id=args.rater_id, sheet_url=args.sheet_url, task_ids=args.tasks)
    print(json.dumps({key: receipt[key] for key in
                      ("status", "task_count", "artifact_count", "empty_artifact_count", "archive_path", "archive_sha256")}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

115	class Budget:
116	    """Conservative ledger: no completed usage means no reservation refund."""
117	
118	    def __init__(self, path):
119	        self.path = Path(path)
120	        if self.path.exists():

124	                     "input_price_per_million": INPUT_PRICE * 1_000_000,
125	                     "output_price_per_million": OUTPUT_PRICE * 1_000_000,
126	                     "requests": [], "denials": []}
127	        self.started = time.monotonic()
128	        self.save()

130	    def save(self):
131	        self.data["accounted_usd"] = sum(
132	            r.get("charged_upper_bound_usd", r["reserved_usd"])
133	            for r in self.data["requests"])
134	        write_json(self.path, self.data)

136	    def reserve(self, tokens, output_tokens, payload_hash):
137	        if time.monotonic() - self.started >= WALL_SECONDS:
138	            raise ValueError("Wall-clock budget exhausted")
139	        if len(self.data["requests"]) >= REQUEST_CAP:
140	            raise ValueError("Provider request cap reached")
141	        if not 0 < tokens <= INPUT_TOKEN_CAP:
142	            raise ValueError("Input token cap exceeded")
143	        if not 0 < output_tokens <= OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP:
144	            raise ValueError("Output token cap exceeded")
145	        # Google countTokens excludes earlier thinking that generateContent
146	        # bills in subsequent promptTokenCount. Keep all prior billed thoughts
147	        # in the admission bound; do not silently treat countTokens as billing.
148	        prior_thoughts = sum(int(r.get("usage_metadata", {}).get("thoughtsTokenCount", 0))
149	                             for r in self.data["requests"])
150	        input_admission_bound = tokens + prior_thoughts + max(1024, (tokens + 9) // 10)
151	        if input_admission_bound > INPUT_TOKEN_CAP:

153	        if any(r.get("provider_finish_reason") is None for r in self.data["requests"]):
154	            raise ValueError("Earlier provider response incomplete; new admission stopped")

156	        # is also reserved/charged at full price. Only complete actual usage
157	        # releases unused reservation; incomplete responses keep it all.
158	        reserved_input = INPUT_TOKEN_CAP

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run one frozen, source-only native Pi cell with an external cost gateway.

The solver container has only an internal Docker network. A separate gateway
container owns the provider key and admits only the frozen Google model. No
repository/home/gold volume is mounted. A failed cell is never retried here.

Prepare a manifest with `manifest`; freeze its printed SHA-256 in the parent
protocol, then pass it to `run --manifest-sha256`. `gateway` is an internal
subcommand used by the runner, not a general proxy. All receipts are private.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import http.server
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone

MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash"
PROVIDER = "allen-google-veribench"
PI_VERSION = "1.5.2"
INPUT_PRICE = 0.75 / 1_000_000
OUTPUT_PRICE = 3.75 / 1_000_000
CELL_CAP = 0.75
REQUEST_CAP = 40
INPUT_TOKEN_CAP = 65_536
OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP = 16_384
WALL_SECONDS = 1800
WORKSPACE = "/home/user/lean_project"
API_ROOT = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta"
MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 4_000_000


def now():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def sha256(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def write_json(path, obj):
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
    temp.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    temp.replace(path)


def safe_relative(name):
    p = PurePosixPath(name)
    if not name or p.is_absolute() or ".." in p.parts or "." == name:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsafe relative path: {name!r}")
    return name


def freeze_input(args):
    root = Path(args.input_dir).resolve()
    paths = sorted(p for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
    if not paths or any(p.is_symlink() for p in root.rglob("*")):
        raise ValueError("Inputs must contain regular files and no symlinks")
    files = {str(p.relative_to(root)): sha256(p.read_bytes()) for p in paths}
    if args.prompt_file not in files:
        raise ValueError("Prompt file is not in input directory")
    safe_relative(args.output_file)
    if args.output_file in files:
        raise ValueError("Output must not exist among frozen inputs")
    manifest = {"task_id": args.task_id, "files": files,
                "prompt_file": args.prompt_file, "output_file": args.output_file,
                "source_only_approval": args.source_only_approval}
    write_json(args.manifest, manifest)
    print(json.dumps({"manifest": str(Path(args.manifest).resolve()),
                      "sha256": sha256(Path(args.manifest).read_bytes()),
                      "files": len(files)}))


def validate_manifest(path, expected_hash, root):
    raw = Path(path).read_bytes()
    if sha256(raw) != expected_hash:
        raise ValueError("Frozen manifest hash mismatch")
    manifest = json.loads(raw)
    if manifest.get("source_only_approval") is not True:
        raise ValueError("Manifest lacks source-only input approval")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", manifest["task_id"]):
        raise ValueError("Invalid task ID")
    files = manifest["files"]
    if not files or manifest["prompt_file"] not in files:
        raise ValueError("Manifest has no input/prompt")
    for name, expected in files.items():
        safe_relative(name)
        source = root / name
        if source.is_symlink() or not source.resolve().is_relative_to(root):
            raise ValueError(f"Input escapes source directory: {name}")
        if sha256(source.read_bytes()) != expected:
            raise ValueError(f"Input hash mismatch: {name}")
    safe_relative(manifest["output_file"])
    if manifest["output_file"] in files:
        raise ValueError("Output already exists among input files")
    return manifest


class Budget:
    """Conservative ledger: no completed usage means no reservation refund."""

    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = Path(path)
        if self.path.exists():
            raise ValueError("Ledger exists; each cell permits one attempt")
        self.data = {"started_at": now(), "model": MODEL,
                     "provider_route": PROVIDER, "cap_usd": CELL_CAP,
                     "input_price_per_million": INPUT_PRICE * 1_000_000,
                     "output_price_per_million": OUTPUT_PRICE * 1_000_000,
                     "requests": [], "denials": []}
        self.started = time.monotonic()
        self.save()

    def save(self):
        self.data["accounted_usd"] = sum(
            r.get("charged_upper_bound_usd", r["reserved_usd"])
            for r in self.data["requests"])
        write_json(self.path, self.data)

    def reserve(self, tokens, output_tokens, payload_hash):
        if time.monotonic() - self.started >= WALL_SECONDS:
            raise ValueError("Wall-clock budget exhausted")
        if len(self.data["requests"]) >= REQUEST_CAP:
            raise ValueError("Provider request cap reached")
        if not 0 < tokens <= INPUT_TOKEN_CAP:
            raise ValueError("Input token cap exceeded")
        if not 0 < output_tokens <= OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP:
            raise ValueError("Output token cap exceeded")
        # Google countTokens excludes earlier thinking that generateContent
        # bills in subsequent promptTokenCount. Keep all prior billed thoughts
        # in the admission bound; do not silently treat countTokens as billing.
        prior_thoughts = sum(int(r.get("usage_metadata", {}).get("thoughtsTokenCount", 0))
                             for r in self.data["requests"])
        input_admission_bound = tokens + prior_thoughts + max(1024, (tokens + 9) // 10)
        if input_admission_bound > INPUT_TOKEN_CAP:
            raise ValueError("Input token cap exceeded")
        if any(r.get("provider_finish_reason") is None for r in self.data["requests"]):
            raise ValueError("Earlier provider response incomplete; new admission stopped")
        # Reserve the FULL input capacity, not just the estimate. Cached input
        # is also reserved/charged at full price. Only complete actual usage
        # releases unused reservation; incomplete responses keep it all.
        reserved_input = INPUT_TOKEN_CAP
        reserved = reserved_input * INPUT_PRICE + output_tokens * OUTPUT_PRICE
        if self.data["accounted_usd"] + reserved > CELL_CAP + 1e-12:
            raise ValueError("Cell dollar cap cannot admit next request")
        row = {"call": len(self.data["requests"]) + 1,
               "admitted_at": now(), "counted_input_tokens": tokens,
               "prior_billed_thought_tokens": prior_thoughts,
               "input_admission_bound": input_admission_bound,
               "reserved_input_tokens": reserved_input,
               "max_output_tokens": output_tokens, "reserved_usd": reserved,
               "payload_sha256": payload_hash}
        self.data["requests"].append(row)
        self.save()
        return row

    def settle(self, row, usage, version, status, finish_reason=None):
        row["finished_at"] = now()
        row["http_status"] = status
        row["model_version"] = version
        row["provider_finish_reason"] = finish_reason
        if usage and "promptTokenCount" in usage:
            prompt = int(usage["promptTokenCount"])
            output = int(usage.get("candidatesTokenCount", 0)) + int(usage.get("thoughtsTokenCount", 0))
            row["usage_metadata"] = usage
            observed = prompt * INPUT_PRICE + output * OUTPUT_PRICE
            row["observed_cost_upper_bound_usd"] = observed
            if (prompt <= row["reserved_input_tokens"] and output <= row["max_output_tokens"]
                    and status == 200 and finish_reason is not None):
                row["charged_upper_bound_usd"] = observed
            else:
                row["provider_cap_violation"] = True
                row["charged_upper_bound_usd"] = max(row["reserved_usd"], observed)
        self.save()


def validated_payload(data):
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "contents" not in data:
        raise ValueError("Expected native Google generateContent payload")
    if data.get("cachedContent"):
        raise ValueError("External cached content is not an allowed input")
    if set(data) - {"contents", "systemInstruction", "tools", "toolConfig", "generationConfig", "safetySettings"}:
        raise ValueError("Unexpected provider payload field")
    config = data.setdefault("generationConfig", {})
    requested = config.get("maxOutputTokens", OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP)
    if not isinstance(requested, int) or isinstance(requested, bool) or not 0 < requested <= OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP:
        raise ValueError("Output token limit differs from frozen cap")
    config["maxOutputTokens"] = requested
    if config.get("candidateCount", 1) != 1:
        raise ValueError("Exactly one candidate per native Pi request")
    if str(config.get("thinkingConfig", {}).get("thinkingLevel", "")).upper() != "HIGH":
        raise ValueError("Expected frozen HIGH thinking setting")
    for tool in data.get("tools", []):
        if set(tool) - {"functionDeclarations"}:
            raise ValueError("Only native Pi function tools are allowed")
    return data, requested


def serve_gateway(args):
    # Prices are frozen at the verified 11-11-2026 standard rate. Fail closed
    # after the announced price-change date rather than silently underbudget.
    if datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat() >= "2027-01-01":
        raise ValueError("Frozen provider price expired; new protocol required")
    key = os.environ.pop("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
    if not key:
        raise ValueError("Gateway requires runtime GEMINI_API_KEY")
    budget = Budget(args.ledger)

    class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        protocol_version = "HTTP/1.0"

        def log_message(self, *_):
            pass

        def fail(self, status, message):
            body = json.dumps({"error": {"code": status, "message": message}}).encode()
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def do_GET(self):
            if self.path == "/health":
                self.send_response(200)
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(b"ready")
            else:
                self.fail(404, "Unsupported gateway route")

        def do_POST(self):
            row = None
            usage = None
            version = None
            finish_reason = None
            status = 502
            response_started = False
            try:
                parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(self.path)
                expected = f"/v1beta/models/{MODEL}:streamGenerateContent"
                if parsed.path != expected or urllib.parse.parse_qs(parsed.query) != {"alt": ["sse"]}:
                    raise ValueError("Provider model/operation differs from frozen condition")
                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
                if not 0 < length <= MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES:
                    raise ValueError("Invalid or excessive payload size")
                data, output_limit = validated_payload(json.loads(self.rfile.read(length)))
                if any(r.get("provider_cap_violation") for r in budget.data["requests"]):
                    raise ValueError("Earlier provider cap violation; cell stopped")
                if len(budget.data["requests"]) >= REQUEST_CAP:
                    raise ValueError("Provider request cap reached")
                count_body = {"generateContentRequest": {"model": f"models/{MODEL}", **data}}
                request = urllib.request.Request(
                    f"{API_ROOT}/models/{MODEL}:countTokens",
                    data=json.dumps(count_body).encode(),
                    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "x-goog-api-key": key})
                with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
                    tokens = int(json.load(response)["totalTokens"])
                body = json.dumps(data, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
                row = budget.reserve(tokens, output_limit, sha256(body))
                request = urllib.request.Request(
                    API_ROOT + self.path[len("/v1beta"):], data=body,
                    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "x-goog-api-key": key})
                with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=180) as response:
                    status = response.status
                    self.send_response(status)
                    self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
                    self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
                    self.end_headers()
                    response_started = True
                    client_connected = True
                    for line in response:
                        if line.startswith(b"data: "):
                            try:
                                event = json.loads(line[6:])
                                usage = event.get("usageMetadata", usage)
                                version = event.get("modelVersion", version)
                                for candidate in event.get("candidates", []):
                                    finish_reason = candidate.get("finishReason", finish_reason)
                            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                                pass
                        if client_connected:
                            try:
                                self.wfile.write(line)
                                self.wfile.flush()
                            except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):
                                client_connected = False
            except Exception as exc:
                # Never log provider error bodies, URLs with credentials, or
                # exception strings that might include sensitive headers.
                reason = str(exc) if isinstance(exc, ValueError) else type(exc).__name__
                budget.data["denials"].append({"at": now(), "reason": reason})
                budget.save()
                if not response_started:
                    try:
                        self.fail(429 if isinstance(exc, ValueError) else 502, reason)
                    except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):
                        pass
            finally:
                if row is not None:
                    budget.settle(row, usage, version, status, finish_reason)

    # HTTPServer serializes requests, preventing concurrent budget reservations.
    http.server.HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", args.port), Handler).serve_forever()


def docker(*args, **kwargs):
    return subprocess.run(["docker", *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, **kwargs)


def run_cell(args):
    root = Path(args.input_dir).resolve()
    manifest = validate_manifest(args.manifest, args.manifest_sha256, root)
    if not re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", args.image):
        raise ValueError("Use the verified immutable Docker image ID")
    out = Path(args.output_dir).resolve()
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lock = out / "attempt_started.json"
    with lock.open("x") as f:
        json.dump({"at": now(), "task_id": manifest["task_id"], "manifest_sha256": args.manifest_sha256}, f)
    image_info = json.loads(docker("image", "inspect", args.image).stdout)[0]
    # Scientific isolation relies on the accepted source-only image plus no
    # host/repository mounts and an internal-only network for the solver.
    receipt = {"started_at": now(), "task_id": manifest["task_id"],
               "manifest_sha256": args.manifest_sha256, "input_files": manifest["files"],
               "model": MODEL, "thinking": "high", "provider_route": PROVIDER,
               "pi_version_required": PI_VERSION, "image_id": image_info["Id"],
               "runner_sha256": sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()),
               "cell_cap_usd": CELL_CAP, "batch_25_cell_cap_usd": 25 * CELL_CAP,
               "request_cap": REQUEST_CAP, "input_token_cap": INPUT_TOKEN_CAP,
               "output_token_cap": OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP, "wall_seconds": WALL_SECONDS,
               "attempts": 1, "status": "preparing", "host_mounts": []}
    write_json(out / "receipt.json", receipt)
    suffix = sha256((str(out) + str(time.time_ns())).encode())[:12]
    network, gateway, solver = (f"ttj-pi-{x}-{suffix}" for x in ("net", "gateway", "solver"))
    created = []
    try:
        if not os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            raise ValueError("Set GEMINI_API_KEY at runtime; runner never writes it to disk")
        docker("network", "create", "--internal", network)
        created.append(("network", network))
        # The gateway can reach Google. The solver can only reach this gateway.
        docker("create", "--name", gateway, "--network", "bridge", "--user", "root",
               "--env", "GEMINI_API_KEY", args.image, "python3", "/tmp/pi_runner.py",
               "gateway", "--ledger", "/tmp/gateway_ledger.json", env=os.environ.copy())
        created.append(("container", gateway))
        docker("network", "connect", "--alias", "provider-gateway", network, gateway)
        docker("cp", str(Path(__file__).resolve()), gateway + ":/tmp/pi_runner.py")
        docker("start", gateway)
        docker("create", "--name", solver, "--network", network,
               "--user", "user", "--workdir", WORKSPACE,
               "--env", "PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/pi-profile",
               "--env", "PI_OFFLINE=1", "--env", "PI_TELEMETRY=0",
               args.image, "sleep", "infinity")
        created.append(("container", solver))
        docker("start", solver)
        # A task-free image must not retain compiled benchmark modules from
        # its source project. Dependency caches are allowed; project caches
        # are not. Check before copying this cell's source files.
        clean_check = (
            "from pathlib import Path; "
            "p=Path('/home/user/lean_project'); "
            "assert not (p/'.git').exists(), 'project Git history present'; "
            "assert not (p/'.lake/build').exists(), 'compiled project artifacts present'; "
            "assert not any(x.is_file() for x in (p/'Veribench').rglob('*')), 'old task artifacts present'; "
            "unexpected=[str(x.relative_to(p)) for x in p.rglob('*') if x.is_file() "
            "and not str(x.relative_to(p)).startswith('.lake/packages/') "
            "and str(x.relative_to(p)) not in {'lakefile.toml','lakefile.lean','lake-manifest.json','lean-toolchain'} "
            "and not str(x.relative_to(p)).startswith('.lake/lakefile.')]; "
            "assert not unexpected, 'unexpected project payload: '+repr(unexpected[:10]); "
            "print('clean source-only project')"
        )
        docker("exec", solver, "python3", "-c", clean_check)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ttj-pi-stage-") as temp:
            stage = Path(temp)
            inputs = stage / "inputs"
            for name in manifest["files"]:
                destination = inputs / name
                destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(root / name, destination)
            profile = stage / "pi-profile"
            profile.mkdir()
            write_json(profile / "settings.json", {
                "defaultProvider": PROVIDER, "defaultModel": MODEL,
                "defaultThinkingLevel": "high", "cacheWarming": "off",
                "compaction": {"enabled": False},
                "retry": {"enabled": False, "maxRetries": 0,
                          "provider": {"maxRetries": 0, "timeoutMs": 180000}}})
            write_json(profile / "models.json", {"providers": {PROVIDER: {
                "baseUrl": "http://provider-gateway:8765/v1beta",
                "api": "google-generative-ai", "apiKey": "gateway-no-provider-secret",
                "models": [{"id": MODEL, "name": "Gemini 3.8 Flash (Allen VeriBench)",
                            "reasoning": True, "input": ["text"],
                            "contextWindow": INPUT_TOKEN_CAP, "maxTokens": OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP,
                            "cost": {"input": 0.75, "output": 3.75,
                                     "cacheRead": 0.75, "cacheWrite": 0}}]}}})
            docker("cp", str(profile), solver + ":/tmp/pi-profile")
            docker("cp", str(inputs) + "/.", solver + ":" + WORKSPACE + "/")
        docker("exec", "--user", "root", solver, "chown", "-R", "user:user", "/tmp/pi-profile")
        # Keep the exact runtime user aligned with the accepted library Git
        # ownership. Lake can delete an otherwise valid checkout after Git's
        # dubious-ownership check prevents it from reading the origin URL.
        runtime_uid = docker("exec", solver, "id", "-u").stdout.strip()
        if runtime_uid != "1001":
            raise ValueError("Expected accepted image runtime user UID1001")
        receipt["runtime_uid"] = int(runtime_uid)
        version = docker("exec", solver, "pi", "--version").stdout.strip()
        receipt["pi_version_observed"] = version
        if version != PI_VERSION:
            raise ValueError("Native Pi version mismatch")
        isolation = json.loads(docker("inspect", solver).stdout)[0]
        if isolation["Mounts"] or set(isolation["NetworkSettings"]["Networks"]) != {network}:
            raise ValueError("Solver mounts/network differ from source-only contract")
        if not json.loads(docker("network", "inspect", network).stdout)[0]["Internal"]:
            raise ValueError("Solver network is not internal-only")
        # Wait for an actual responding gateway, not merely a live process.
        health = ["exec", solver, "python3", "-c",
                  "import urllib.request; print(urllib.request.urlopen('http://provider-gateway:8765/health',timeout=3).read().decode())"]
        for _ in range(30):
            try:
                if docker(*health).stdout.strip() == "ready":
                    break
            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
                time.sleep(0.5)
        else:
            raise ValueError("Provider gateway did not become ready")
        receipt["status"] = "running"
        write_json(out / "receipt.json", receipt)
        command = ["docker", "exec", solver, "pi", "--provider", PROVIDER,
                   "--model", MODEL, "--thinking", "high", "--mode", "json", "--print",
                   "--no-context-files", "--no-extensions", "--no-mcp", "--no-skills",
                   "--no-prompt-templates", "--no-themes", "--offline", "--no-approve",
                   "--tools", "read,bash,edit,write", "--session-dir", "/tmp/pi-sessions",
                   "@" + WORKSPACE + "/" + manifest["prompt_file"]]
        started = time.monotonic()
        with (out / "trajectory.jsonl").open("wb") as stdout, (out / "stderr.log").open("wb") as stderr:
            process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr)
            try:
                code = process.wait(timeout=WALL_SECONDS)
                receipt["status"] = "process_completed" if code == 0 else "process_failed"
                receipt["exit_code"] = code
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                receipt["status"] = "timeout"
                docker("stop", "--time", "2", solver)
                process.wait(timeout=15)
        receipt["elapsed_seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
        # Native Pi can return process exit code zero after provider errors.
        # Preserve its semantic terminal status rather than claiming success.
        assistant_messages = []
        for line in (out / "trajectory.jsonl").read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            try:
                event = json.loads(line)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if event.get("type") == "message_end" and event.get("message", {}).get("role") == "assistant":
                assistant_messages.append(event["message"])
        if assistant_messages:
            final = assistant_messages[-1]
            receipt["native_stop_reason"] = final.get("stopReason")
            receipt["actual_model"] = final.get("model")
            receipt["actual_provider"] = final.get("provider")
            receipt["actual_thinking"] = final.get("thinkingLevel")
            if receipt["status"] == "process_completed" and final.get("stopReason") in {"error", "aborted"}:
                receipt["status"] = "provider_error"
        elif receipt["status"] == "process_completed":
            receipt["status"] = "no_assistant_response"
        # A timeout/failed process can still leave an artifact: preserve it, never
        # relabel it as successful just because a file exists.
        candidate = out / "candidate.lean"
        try:
            docker("cp", solver + ":" + WORKSPACE + "/" + manifest["output_file"], str(candidate))
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            receipt["artifact_status"] = "missing"
        else:
            if candidate.is_symlink() or not candidate.is_file():
                receipt["artifact_status"] = "invalid_nonregular_file"
            else:
                data = candidate.read_bytes()
                receipt["artifact_status"] = "present" if data.strip() else "empty"
                receipt["artifact_sha256"] = sha256(data)
                receipt["artifact_bytes"] = len(data)
                receipt["candidate_file"] = "candidate.lean"
        try:
            docker("cp", solver + ":/tmp/pi-sessions", str(out / "pi-sessions"))
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            pass
    except Exception as exc:
        receipt["status"] = "runner_error"
        receipt["error_type"] = type(exc).__name__
        if isinstance(exc, ValueError):
            receipt["error"] = str(exc)
        raise
    finally:
        try:
            docker("cp", gateway + ":/tmp/gateway_ledger.json", str(out / "gateway_ledger.json"))
            ledger = json.loads((out / "gateway_ledger.json").read_text())
            receipt["provider_requests"] = len(ledger["requests"])
            receipt["accounted_usd"] = ledger["accounted_usd"]
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
            pass
        receipt["finished_at"] = now()
        write_json(out / "receipt.json", receipt)
        for kind, name in reversed(created):
            subprocess.run(["docker", kind, "rm", "-f", name] if kind == "container"
                           else ["docker", "network", "rm", name], capture_output=True)
    print(json.dumps(receipt, sort_keys=True))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    manifest = sub.add_parser("manifest", help="Write source allowlist for parent freezing")
    manifest.add_argument("--input-dir", required=True)
    manifest.add_argument("--task-id", required=True)
    manifest.add_argument("--prompt-file", required=True)
    manifest.add_argument("--output-file", default="candidate.lean")
    manifest.add_argument("--source-only-approval", action="store_true")
    manifest.add_argument("--manifest", required=True)
    run = sub.add_parser("run", help="Execute exactly one frozen cell")
    for name in ("input-dir", "manifest", "manifest-sha256", "image", "output-dir"):
        run.add_argument("--" + name, required=True)
    gateway = sub.add_parser("gateway", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    gateway.add_argument("--ledger", required=True)
    gateway.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8765)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    {"manifest": freeze_input, "run": run_cell, "gateway": serve_gateway}[args.command](args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
